page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor using the ARM64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, alongside a 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. Networking is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results place the c7gd.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall within the middle 50% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 775.35 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 148.04 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, the server exhibits weak performance in Passmark CPU encryption and overall Passmark CPU score. LLM inference benchmarks show average text generation speeds for small and medium models, but poor prompt processing speeds for medium 7B models.

This instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that require fast local storage but do not demand large memory capacities. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated physical cores minimize resource contention. Tradeoffs include the lack of AVX instruction support and weaker cryptographic performance. The server is suited for workloads such as software compilation, text and image processing, static web serving, and database operations that leverage the local NVMe SSD.
